record.paper_title: Some open problems in random matrix theory and the theory of integrable systems
record.original_question: Determine the long-time behavior of integrable systems when the initial data are non-generic and the associated Lax operator has singular spectral features not covered by the standard generic theory. In particular, for focusing nonlinear Schrödinger evolution, understand how spectra that accumulate on the real line at essentially arbitrary rates affect long-time asymptotics, and similarly clarify the situation for higher-order self-adjoint Lax operators such as those for the Boussinesq equation.

evidence.quote: It is a very interesting question to determine what effect such singularities would have on the long-time behavior of the solution of NLS.
The long-time behavior of the solutions of the Boussinesq equation with general initial data is a very interesting problem with many challenges.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) equation
  i q_t + q_{xx} + 2|q|^2 q = 0,  (x,t) ∈ ℝ × ℝ_+,
with initial data q(x,0) = q_0(x) decaying as |x| → ∞. The associated Lax operator is the Zakharov–Shabat operator
  L = i σ_3 (∂_x − Q(x)),  Q(x) = ((0, q_0(x)),(−\bar q_0(x), 0)),
whose spectral data (reflection coefficient and discrete eigenvalues) determine q(x,t) via inverse scattering.

The standard nonlinear steepest-descent theory yields detailed long-time asymptotics under "generic" assumptions on q_0 (e.g., reflection coefficient smooth on ℝ, finitely many simple discrete eigenvalues off ℝ, no spectral singularities). 

(a) Suppose q_0 is non-generic in the sense that the discrete spectrum (or, more generally, spectral singularities of L) accumulates on the real axis at an essentially arbitrary prescribed rate. Determine the leading-order long-time behavior of q(x,t) in each region of the (x,t)-plane, expressed in terms of this accumulation rate.

(b) Consider the Boussinesq equation
  u_{tt} = u_{xxxx} + (u^2)_{xx},
which admits a self-adjoint Lax operator of order three. For general (non-generic) decaying initial data (u(x,0), u_t(x,0)), determine the long-time asymptotic behavior of the solution u(x,t).

The problem is to provide rigorous asymptotic formulas (with error estimates) covering these non-generic settings that are not handled by the existing generic theory.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed several non-generic cases for focusing NLS: long-time asymptotics in the presence of real spectral singularities have been derived (with O((log t/t)^{1/2}) corrections near stationary phase points), and asymptotics in the solitonic region with high-order discrete eigenvalues have been obtained via Riemann–Hilbert/steepest-descent methods. For the Boussinesq equation, long-time asymptotics for Schwartz-class initial data have been studied. However, the full problem—covering arbitrary accumulation rates of eigenvalues to the real line for focusing NLS, and general (non-generic) initial data for Boussinesq—remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Long time behavior for the focusing NLS equation with real spectral singularities
status_evidence.snippet: The effect of real spectral singularities on long-time behavior is limited to regions where a spectral singularity is close to the stationary phase point; decay O((log t/t)^{1/2}).
status_evidence.claim: Spectral-singularity case for focusing NLS has been analyzed, giving partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Long time asymptotics for focusing NLS with high-order discrete spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Steepest descent applied to the Cauchy problem of focusing NLS with non-generic initial data allowing high-order discrete spectrum; long-time asymptotic expression in the solitonic region obtained.
status_evidence.claim: Non-generic cases with high-order poles have been treated.

status_evidence.title: Long-time asymptotics for the Boussinesq equation
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlinear steepest descent applied to Boussinesq with Schwartz-class initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Boussinesq long-time asymptotics studied for restricted classes of data, not in full generality.
